brief.headline: Russia claims Konstantinovka; ramps fuel-infrastructure strike campaign
brief.lead: The monitored channels coalesced around a claimed capture of Konstantinovka paired with a publicized offer to return Ukrainian bodies, alongside a sustained narrative of crippling strikes on Ukrainian fuel and rail logistics; tone was upbeat overall (63% positive) but sharply negative toward the West and toward Ukrainian strikes on Russia.

developments.title: Channels claim Konstantinovka captured, offer body-retrieval ceasefire
developments.body: Rybar, WarGonzo and Kotsnews claimed Russian forces completed the 'liberation' of Konstantinovka after months of urban combat, though Rybar admitted small Ukrainian groups remain in cellars during ongoing mop-up. Multiple channels amplified a Russian proposal for a humanitarian pause to transfer fallen Ukrainian soldiers with foreign media watching—claims are unconfirmed and framed to pressure Kyiv into implicitly conceding the city's loss.

developments.title: Sustained strikes claimed on Ukrainian fuel, power and rail
developments.body: The dominant strikes narrative (22 posts) claimed systematic destruction of Ukrainian fuel stations, gas compressor stations, substations and rail logistics; Kotsnews claimed 150+ fuel stations destroyed in two months, and channels cited a Geran-4 hitting a 110kV substation in Diakivka, Sumy. Notably, Two Majors and others conceded strikes 'often hit non-critical equipment rather than fuel storage tanks,' a rare self-critical note.

developments.title: Anti-Western sentiment sharpens across NATO topic
developments.body: West & NATO coverage ran heavily negative (net -62), with Rybar dismissing IISS claims of Russian drone reconnaissance over NATO nuclear sites as fabrication and flagging $4bn US upgrades to UK bases. Two Majors claimed the US provided targeting intelligence for deep strikes including a Moscow refinery and mocked Kyiv for painting a Kyiv statue in US flag colors on July 4.

developments.title: Channels acknowledge Ukrainian strikes on Crimea, Rostov, LNR
developments.body: In rare negative-tone posts, Two Majors reported overnight Ukrainian strikes creating 'serious energy supply problems' for Crimea and Sevastopol, plus drone/missile attacks on Rostov region infrastructure. WarGonzo claimed a Ukrainian drone killed a 57-year-old civilian driver in Kreminna, LNR. All unverified.

developments.title: FSB claims 87 disrupted Ukrainian operations, minors recruited
developments.body: Rybar amplified an FSB claim of disrupting 87 Ukrainian intelligence operations in the first half of 2026, asserting many involved minors recruited as saboteurs against military and infrastructure targets—an MoD/security-service-sourced, unconfirmed claim feeding an internal-threat narrative.

developments.title: Putin-Trump call reported alongside Konstantinovka framing
developments.body: Kotsnews reported a Putin-Trump phone call discussing the battlefield and naming Konstantinovka as an important Russian objective, tying the diplomatic channel to the day's claimed territorial gain. Framing suggests channels want the call read as tacit US acknowledgment of Russian momentum.

narrative_watch.title: 'Ukraine treats its dead as expendable'
narrative_watch.body: Multiple channels built a moralizing frame around Kyiv's alleged refusal to retrieve bodies from Konstantinovka, using it to imply territorial concession and portray Russia as the humane actor.

narrative_watch.title: Economic-attrition strike doctrine
narrative_watch.body: Channels increasingly frame fuel, power and rail strikes as a deliberate campaign to collapse Ukraine's economic base and logistics, mirroring their complaints about Ukraine's own refinery strikes.

narrative_watch.title: Domestic self-criticism on info-space and strike accuracy
narrative_watch.body: Starshe Eddy urged officials to fight narratives on 'forbidden' Instagram rather than retreat, while several channels admitted strikes miss fuel tanks—an unusually candid internal-critique thread.

mood_lines.text: Strongly positive (net +82); triumphalist over fuel/rail/power strikes, with rare admissions that many hits miss critical fuel storage.
Uniformly positive (net +100), driven by the claimed Konstantinovka capture and advances near Sumy and Zaporizhzhia.
Sharply negative (net -62, moved 26); anger at US intelligence-sharing, UK base upgrades and IISS reconnaissance claims dismissed as fabrication.
Fully negative (net -100); grudging acknowledgment of Crimea energy problems, Rostov damage and a civilian death in LNR.
Turned positive (net +29, moved 37) on FSB counter-sabotage claims and body-armor testing, tempered by drone-threat and info-space worries.
Negative (net -100), narrowly focused on Kyiv's refusal to collect its soldiers' bodies from Konstantinovka.

flag_texts.title: West & NATO sentiment drops (net -62, move 26)
flag_texts.body: NATO coverage soured on claims of US intelligence-sharing for deep strikes into Russia, $4bn UK base upgrades, and Kyiv's July 4 statue gesture, deepening an already hostile frame.

flag_texts.title: Russia internal sentiment rises (net +29, move 37)
flag_texts.body: Internal topic swung positive on FSB claims of disrupting 87 Ukrainian operations and successful body-armor testing, offsetting negative posts on Hornet drone threats and Instagram use.

flag_texts.title: Watchlist topics quiet: mobilisation, Putin criticism
flag_texts.body: No posts on mobilisation rumours or criticism of Putin appeared today; the channels' critical energy was directed outward at Kyiv and the West rather than at Russian leadership.
